sourcesRead.title: Repetitions are not all alike: distinct mechanisms sustain repetition in language models (Mahaut, Franzon; Universitat Pompeu Fabra)

claims.claim: Mahaut and Franzon find that two behaviourally identical repetition loops come from different internal processes, one a learned in-context copying circuit and the other an early-emerging behaviour with no identifiable circuit.
claims.source: Mahaut, Franzon, 'Repetitions are not all alike', arXiv:2504.01100v2 (2025)
claims.quote: this condition lacks a clearly identifiable circuit
claims.modelEra: Pythia 1.4B across training checkpoints, observation 2025; register measured: natural text prompts and in-context learning prompts

claims.claim: Mahaut and Franzon report that during naturally arising repetition the model's attention falls disproportionately on low-information tokens such as punctuation and newlines, which they read as a fallback when the relevant context cannot be retrieved.
claims.modelEra: Pythia 1.4B, 2025; register measured: natural text prompts

claims.claim: Mahaut and Franzon measure that as a repeated context lengthens over more cycles the next-token entropy falls and the probability of the repeated tokens rises.
claims.quote: contexts, encompassing more cycles, correlate with
claims.modelEra: Pythia 1.4B, 1000-token greedy generations, 2025; register measured: natural text and in-context prompts

claims.claim: Mahaut and Franzon conclude that both uncertainty and over-reliance on context can drive a model into repetition, and that the two accounts describe concurrent mechanisms rather than rivals.
claims.quote: overreliance on context can lead to repetition, each
claims.modelEra: Pythia 1.4B, 2025; register measured: natural text and in-context prompts
